movesets.name: Defensive
movesets.description:
Ferrothorn is an excellent defensive Steel-type and entry hazard setter, since its Grass typing lends it resistances to Water and Electric as well as a neutrality to Ground, allowing it to more comfortably handle Pokemon like Ogerpon-W, Mega Swampert, Tapu Koko, and Raging Bolt, which other Steel-types like Mega Scizor and Gholdengo have more trouble against; being a Steel-type also naturally improves its matchup against Melmetal, Tapu Lele, and Rillaboom. Iron Barbs lets Ferrothorn pressure foes like Urshifu-R, Mega Lopunny, Melmetal lacking Protective Pads, and U-turn users like Landorus-T, forcing them to play more carefully lest they rack up chip damage very quickly with contact moves. Leech Seed is Ferrothorn's most reliable recovery, allowing it to pressure other passive Pokemon like Toxapex and Gliscor into wasting their healing moves, deal valuable chip damage to switch-ins that have no means of healing such as Cinderace and Heatran, and gradually recover HP with each use. Knock Off allows Ferrothorn to punish Heavy-Duty Boots users like Zapdos, Toxapex, and Tornadus-T as well as Leftovers users like Landorus-T, which is extremely valuable in forcing progress by making foes more susceptible to hazards or removing their recovery. Body Press allows Ferrothorn to surprise Kingambit and Kyurem, dealing massive damage to both and avoiding getting PP stalled by Kyurem; it also lets Ferrothorn hit Heatran on the switch and damage opposing Ferrothorn instead of idling. Gyro Ball snags Fairy-types like Tapu Lele and Iron Valiant on the switch and is better neutral coverage against foes like Dragonite, although it should be run with a Relaxed nature and 0 Speed IVs. Thunder Wave is niche, providing great value against offense teams, but since it is easily blocked by Gholdengo, it is often undesirable. Spikes is used over Stealth Rock when another setter is present on the team. The Special Defense EVs allow Ferrothorn to survive Choice Specs Tapu Lele's Focus Blast from full HP. Leftovers is nigh mandatory, providing much more consistent healing than Leech Seed and taking advantage of Ferrothorn's ability to sit on the field for many turns at a time. Rocky Helmet is a viable alternative, punishing U-turn users like Landorus-T and Urshifu-R as well as Rapid Spin from Great Tusk much harder; overall, it rewards risky play compared to Leftovers’s relative safety and should therefore allow Ferrothorn to be used more aggressively.

Most wallbreakers pair well with Ferrothorn, taking advantage of the entry hazards it sets to break through defensive targets, but those that switch in on Ferrothorn's counters such as Gholdengo, Zamazenta, and Mega Charizard Y are particularly good; these wallbreakers include Kingambit, Mega Charizard Y, Tapu Lele, and Mega Tyranitar; Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar can also Pursuit trap Gholdengo. Gholdengo itself is also a good teammate, as it can deny Defog and switch in more easily against Pokemon like Tapu Lele and Iron Valiant. Ferrothorn's defensive utility is also appreciated by teammates like Toxapex and Landorus-T, which struggle with Electric-types like Tapu Koko and Water- and Ice-types like Hisuian Samurott and Kyurem, all of which Ferrothorn helps check. However, Ferrothorn does have a host of issues that require some support to cover. Ferrothorn's glaring Fire weakness is not even its biggest problem, given that having teammates like Toxapex, Heatran, and Alomomola around can easily blank Fire-type moves from the likes of Mega Charizard Y and opposing Heatran. Its main problem stems from its lack of instant recovery, making it more inclined to offensively oriented teams. Having Leftovers removed by Knock Off from foes like Kingambit, Mega Tyranitar, and opposing Ferrothorn or getting burned by Scald from foes like Toxapex renders it unable to heal without Leech Seed, and Leech Seed fails against Gholdengo and common Grass-types like Ogerpon-W and opposing Ferrothorn. Therefore, Ferrothorn is best played more offensively, using its unique defensive utility, Leech Seed, and Iron Barbs to force switches and hazard chip damage, granting immediate momentum when played aggressively while also not punishing the user for playing more carefully. Teammates that can absorb Knock Off, like Mega Tyranitar, and those that can absorb Will-O-Wisp, like Heatran and Clefable, are incredibly valuable teammates. Finally, Pokemon that can cover Ferrothorn's Fighting weakness are good defensively, including the aforementioned Gholdengo as well as Zapdos, Landorus-T, and Toxapex.

movesets.name: Entry Hazard Wall (Grass)
movesets.description:
Ferrothorn is a highly reliable wall in Grass teams, boasting good defensive stats, recovery, and an immunity to Poison. It's an incredible asset for Grass teams, as it can manage notable threats such as Kyurem, Tapu Lele, and Melmetal. Gyro Ball capitalizes on its low Speed and threatens Fairy-types and fast foes like Alolan Ninetales and Tapu Lele. However, Iron Head provides more consistent damage against slower foes like Hatterene and is less susceptible to PP stalling, which is particularly useful against Kyurem if Ferrothorn isn't running Body Press. Depending on its teammates, Ferrothorn can opt for Stealth Rock or Spikes, as Cradily can also set up Stealth Rock, while Meowscarada has access to Spikes and Toxic Spikes. With the combination of Leech Seed and Leftovers, Ferrothorn gains substantial recovery each turn, enabling it to wear down and punish switch-ins such as Heatran, Aegislash, and Nidoking. Protect serves as a scouting tool and extends the benefits of Leech Seed and Leftovers, while Body Press allows Ferrothorn to utilize its high Defense and deal significant damage to Steel- and Dark-types, like Melmetal and Weavile. When in conjunction with Gyro Ball, Body Press ensures that Substitute Kyurem won't be able to PP stall Ferrothorn, and when used with Iron Head, it guarantees an OHKO against Weavile. The featured EV spread both prevents a 2HKO from Choice Band Weavile's Icicle Crash and lets Ferrothorn almost always beat SubRoost Kyurem.

Ferrothorn forms a formidable defensive core with Mega Venusaur, as the latter's typing and ability enable it to come in on Fighting- and Ice-types such as Iron Valiant, Iron Moth, and Galarian Darmanitan. Additionally, Mega Venusaur's Sludge Bomb can poison foes, allowing Ferrothorn's combination of Leech Seed and Protect to wear them down more quickly. Cradily is another valuable partner, providing natural special bulk and a favorable matchup against Blacephalon and Nidoking. Offensive partners such as Rillaboom, Meowscarada, Iron Leaves, and Zarude greatly appreciate Ferrothorn weakening the opposing team with entry hazards and Leech Seed. In return, Rillaboom sets up Grassy Terrain for additional recovery and provides strong priority damage, while Choice Scarf Meowscarada can revenge kill threats such as boosted Kommo-o. Whimsicott and Celebi handle Fighting-types such as Iron Valiant and Kommo-o, which would otherwise pose a threat to Ferrothorn. Whimsicott also punishes setup sweepers like Volcarona or Mega Scizor, which could otherwise use Ferrothorn as setup fodder, while Celebi helps ease the Poison matchup, as well as the Steel matchup in a pinch.

movesets.name: Hazard Setter (Steel)
movesets.description: As a check to Water- and Ground-types that can support its team with a wide variety of utility options, Ferrothorn is a notable defensive asset for Steel teams. Protect allows Ferrothorn to maximize the HP it gains per turn between Leftovers and Leech Seed, as well as easing prediction against Choice-locked foes such as Enamorus, Galarian Darmanitan, and Hisuian Arcanine. Power Whip minimizes passivity against the foes it's meant to check, notably OHKOing Mega Swampert and Gastrodon. Knock Off provides utility by removing Heavy-Duty Boots from foes such as Volcarona, Mantine, and Victini, leaving them vulnerable to the entry hazard stacking that is characteristic of Steel teams. The given EV spread with a Careful nature avoids a 2HKO from Landorus's Earth Power, with the rest invested in Defense to ease checking foes such as Mega Swampert, Ogerpon-W, and Mega Aerodactyl. The alternate EV spread with an Impish nature instead maximizes physical bulk, notably avoiding a 2HKO from Ogerpon-C's Low Kick. As Ferrothorn is easy to force out by Fire-type moves, Heatran is a solid partner to make a defensive core with it, especially because it can also set Stealth Rock, allowing Ferrothorn to run Spikes to hazard stack further; this can be further complemented with a check to Fighting-types in Gholdengo, which keeps entry hazards set by Ferrothorn on the other side of the field by blocking hazard removal. Offensive Pokemon such as Mega Scizor and Excadrill benefit from Ferrothorn wearing down and hindering the opposing team for a late-game sweep, mitigating Ferrothorn's passivity issues. Chople Berry is a niche alternative over Leftovers, as it enables Ferrothorn to withstand an attack from Fighting-types such as Keldeo and Urshifu-R, then KO back with Power Whip.

movesets.name: Specially Defensive
movesets.description:
• Ferrothorn's stellar typing, high bulk, and rare access to Spikes grant it a unique position in the metagame as the cornerstone of hazard-stacking balance teams over Pokemon such as defensive Necrozma-DM. Ferrothorn serves as a sturdy roadblock to wallbreaker Primal Kyogre, which otherwise easily overwhelms most balance teams. Additionally, Ferrothorn checks Ground-types such as Arceus-Ground and Zygarde. However, Ferrothorn struggles against more offensive teams, as Pokemon such as Zacian-C and Mega Salamence are able to take advantage of Ferrothorn's passivity to use it as setup fodder.
  • Power Whip provides Ferrothorn the means to scare out Pokemon such as Primal Kyogre and Arceus-Ground. Wallbreaker Primal Kyogre is OHKOed after Stealth Rock, and defensive Arceus-Ground is 2HKOed after a single layer of Spikes. Ferrothorn is able to capitalize on the switches it forces to set a layer of Spikes or use Leech Seed to help keep itself healthy. Leech Seed also ensures that Ferrothorn can still defeat defensive Primal Kyogre even when burnt and provides some valuable healing for Pokemon such as Primal Groudon and Giratina-O.
  • Knock Off is preferred in the last moveslot, as many of Ferrothorn's common switch-ins, such as Ho-Oh and Yveltal, are heavily dependent on their items to function. Protect is an alternative that enables Ferrothorn to rack up healing from Leftovers and Leech Seed and scout Choice-locked Pokemon such as Rayquaza, Marshadow, and Lunala, but Protect makes it significantly more passive.
  • A Sassy nature and 0 Speed IVs are used to enable Ferrothorn to outspeed Melmetal under Trick Room. This gives Ferrothorn the flexibility to set a layer of Spikes or Knock Off Melmetal's Choice Band, preventing it from being able to 2HKO Ferrothorn with Tera Steel Double Iron Bash. Ferrothorn maximizes its special bulk to better check wallbreaker Primal Kyogre, as even Water Spout fails to 2HKO.
  • Ferrothorn rarely Terastallizes, as it is reliant on its natural typing to function, but it does benefit from Terastallization in some scenarios. Tera Water swaps Ferrothorn's quadruple Fire weakness for a resistance. While Ferrothorn is not able to meaningfully damage any of the Fire-types in the tier, Tera does enable it to beat Ho-Oh if it is the last Pokemon alive, as Ho-Oh seldom runs recovery and is worn down by Iron Barbs and Leech Seed damage before it is able to knock out Ferrothorn. Tera Grass is an alternative to help Ferrothorn better check Arceus-Ground and Zygarde by turning its neutrality to Ground into a resistance. Tera Grass Power Whip is capable of OHKOing Calm Mind Arceus-Ground after a single layer of Spikes and Leech Seed damage. While Ferrothorn cannot beat Coil Zygarde directly even with Tera Grass, its newfound Ground resistance provides it with extra turns to use Knock Off or Leech Seed before switching to a teammate that can handle Zygarde. Ferrothorn does still have some issues with Dragon Dance Zygarde, however, as it commonly runs Substitute.
  • Ferrothorn is best used in the early- and mid-game to set Spikes against defensive Pokemon such as utility Arceus formes and Alomomola. If Primal Kyogre is on the opposing team, Ferrothorn should prioritize preserving HP until the set is revealed, as it can easily get chipped to where it is unable to switch into wallbreaker Primal Kyogre's Water Spout. Ferrothorn can be used as a lead against hyper offense teams due to its immunity to Smeargle's Spore and Glimmora's Mortal Spin enabling it to break their Focus Sashes easily. Ferrothorn matches up poorly into most hyper offense teams due to its overall passivity, so sacrificing Ferrothorn to deal with suicide leads enables teammates such as Primal Groudon and Arceus-Dark to preserve HP and better handle common threats such as Zacian-C and Ultra Necrozma.
  • Ferrothorn shines against balance and stall teams, as the passive damage it deals racks up over the course of longer games. Many defensive Pokemon are unable to meaningfully damage Ferrothorn, which makes it difficult to wear down. Stall teams in particular have a tough time preventing Ferrothorn from making progress; the only Knock Off absorber, Arceus-Dark, is unable to meaningfully hurt Ferrothorn, as Foul Play activates Iron Barbs. This allows Ferrothorn to keep both itself and its teammates healthy with Leech Seed while freely laying down Spikes.
  • Ferrothorn pairs best with defensive Pokemon that are vulnerable to wallbreaker Primal Kyogre. As such, Zygarde is an excellent teammate for Ferrothorn due to it countering the tier's prominent Fire-types, Primal Groudon and Ho-Oh. Zygarde is also the best blanket physical wall in the tier and is able to help check physical attackers such as Marshadow and Mega Salamence that are able to break Ferrothorn. Defensive Primal Groudon is also an excellent teammate for Ferrothorn, as it can set Stealth Rock and work in conjunction with Ferrothorn to ensure that Primal Kyogre rarely poses a threat. Ferrothorn can check wallbreaker Primal Kyogre, which often overwhelms Primal Groudon and leaves it unable to check Pokemon such as Zacian-C, while Primal Groudon can remove Pokemon such as Ho-Oh and Eternatus that that threaten Ferrothorn.
  • Ferrothorn struggles against Taunt users such as Yveltal and utility Arceus formes. Consequently, Arceus-Fairy is a solid teammate for Ferrothorn, as it counters specially offensive Yveltal and can use Taunt to prevent Ho-Oh, Yveltal, and Giratina-O from removing Ferrothorn's Spikes.
  • Choice Band Marshadow is a decent offensive partner for Ferrothorn due to its ability to revenge kill many Pokemon found on hyper offense teams, including Ultra Necrozma, Deoxys-A, and Zacian-C. Ditto can also fill this role, as it threatens to reverse sweep by copying Pokemon such as Zacian-C and Mega Salamence.
